description: The first family-F28 arm (DECISIONS.md 9.148): the F27 stack with the household car constraint enforced CAR-ONLY. F27's only arm ran under RUN.qsim.vehicle_behavior = wait, which is global in MATSim and stranded walk and taxi (network modes with per-person vehicles, neither chain-based): iteration-0 car departures 82,388 against F26's 232,394 with 55,862 car agents stuck, and by iteration 19 co-evolution had abandoned every plan that strands - stopped at 19, citable for nothing. Now citysim.HouseholdCarDepartureHandler, registered before the netsim engine, holds a driver whose household car is out at the link until MATSim's own link parks the car back and departs them; vehicle_behavior is teleport again for everything else. What the arm must answer, in order. (0) ITERATION 0's legHistogram FIRST: car departures near F26's 232,394 and car stuck near F26's 2,699 say the handler is car-only; the log's `householdCar: N driver(s) waited` says it is doing its one job; a stuck count in the tens of thousands means stop. (a) THE ROSTER (9.146): car legs starting with every household car out (0 expected for one-car households), the wait-time distribution, stuck agents attributable to a car that never came back, and where the 29,827 self-driven bound trips settle - onto ride, walk or pt. (b) THE LISTENER: ride legs on persons with no boundDriver (~0 expected) and the pair rate against F26's 0.7865. (c) RIDE against -41.6%, read TOGETHER with car (+11.5%), walk (-22.7%), bike (+118.1%) and taxi (+157.0%): a real ride gain should draw car down and, if the car-less quarter's excess is ride's deficit (9.123), bike and taxi with it; walk left the band the wrong way at F26 as car took its trips, so the seesaw is the thing to watch. (d) The bound-trip selection rate against F26's 0.455 - the selection half of the lane, which is what remains once the second car is gone. (e) The pt SPLIT as a CONTROL: heavy rail +234.7%, bus +40.5%, light rail -55.9%, ferry -70.5% at F26; nothing here touches pt. (f) CONVERGENCE, requirement 8, still unmeasured: innovation off at 240. (g) The awaiting-run measurements the open issues name: #145, #86, #48, #93, #96, #94, #98, #108, #107, #82, #131, #30, #49, #50, #66. S2 x WEEKDAY at 25%, 300 iterations, innovation off at 240, gated every 100 iterations under the loop in GOAL.md with the runner's own watcher stopping the hard bar itself (9.137) - in which case the arm closes itself out as stopped_at_gate and its reading is citable at its reached_iteration and nowhere past it (9.143). 25% is the standing directive (user, 1 Sep). Cost: MEASURED, not projected - the F26 arm took 38,426 s to iteration 100, a mean 384 s an iteration, of which a tenth was milestone output the monitoring never read (9.147); on the F27 stack the three f27_timing_probe_25pct runs read a plain iteration at 264-272 s with the detour routing parallel and RUN.machine.threads = 16, and a milestone now writes a trips table rather than plans and events, so 300 iterations is nearer ~25 h; `wait` adds waiting agents to the qsim and may move that either way, and this arm's own stopwatch is the measurement of both. Graph rendering is OFF (9.59). NEVER compare this arm with any run before the F27 boundary: the demand (householdVehicles, the carve pool), the plans and the compiled controler are all part of a run's identity (9.127, 9.138, 9.142, 9.143, 9.146). NOTHING THIS PRODUCES IS A RESULT until its record says ran_to_last_iteration.
